facts.text: Ms .45 was made for roughly $62,000, a shoestring even by 1980 standards. Director Abel Ferrara shot it in New York City.
Zoë Lund, who plays the mute seamstress Thana, was only 17 when she shot this, her very first film role.
In the U.S., Ms .45 came out via Rochelle Films. Warner Bros. handled overseas, where it was retitled Angel of Vengeance.
Director Abel Ferrara cast himself as the masked first attacker, wearing a clear plastic mask over makeup, a wink to his earlier film The Driller Killer.
Filming took just four weeks in February and March 1980 on real New York streets, often without official filming permits.
The script by Nicholas St. John was so thin that cinematographer James Lemmo noted it; St. John added dialogue as shooting went on.
The MPAA first slapped Ms .45 with an X rating. Two rape scenes and some explicit dialogue were trimmed to earn an R.
Watch the dead burglar draped over the bathtub: the actor can be spotted breathing, his back rising and falling slightly.
Zoë Lund's character Thana echoes Thanatos, the Greek personification of death. Freud used the word for the human 'death drive'.
Abel Ferrara told composer Joe Delia to write a score that was both modern and atonal, hence the jittery sax-heavy sound.
Screenwriter Nicholas St. John went to high school with director Abel Ferrara and wrote many of his films, including The Driller Killer.
The title says .45, but Thana's pistol is actually a Spanish-made 9mm Star Model BM, a lookalike of the Colt 1911.
One of the body-part shopping bags Thana carries out is from Fiorucci, the trendy New York store of the era.
Zoë Lund said her face is on camera with no dialogue about 98% of the time, so she was heavily involved in shaping the character.
Bogey, the dog who plays Mrs. Nasone's pooch Phil, was rescued from a dog pound.
Zoë Lund went on to co-write and act in Abel Ferrara's 1992 cult classic Bad Lieutenant.
Ms .45 nods to Taxi Driver, Repulsion, Psycho, Carrie and I Spit on Your Grave, a grindhouse revenge mix.
This crowded Fifth Avenue shot was filmed from a tarp-covered van with director Abel Ferrara inside. The couple walking behind are crew hiding the mic under a jacket.
Director Abel Ferrara found Zoë Lund after she placed third for a role in the 1980 film Times Square. She reportedly earned more as a two-night extra on that film than she was paid for Ms .45.
In the studio shooting, the camera whips away and a bearded crew member in a red shirt flashes by, just after fake blood is hurled in from off-camera.
New York Times critic Janet Maslin trashed it in 1981, calling most of the supporting cast 'disastrous' but praising Zoë Lund and Abel Ferrara's direction.
Spot the continuity glitch: as Thana loads a bag into a stranger's trunk, a yellow car parked in front suddenly vanishes several car-lengths away.
Britain's BBFC cut 1m 42s from the 1990s video release, including a bread-knife shot and nunchakus. Some uncut tapes escaped by mistake.
Director Abel Ferrara's best-known works include The Driller Killer, King of New York and Bad Lieutenant.
Shooting with a dog who had no training was one of the headaches on this street-level shoot, says creative consultant Jack McIntyre, who also helped keep the production cheap and moving.
Once hated, Ms .45 now holds 86% on Rotten Tomatoes and is considered a landmark of underground, independent cinema.
Ms .45 got its own full-length book: film scholar Alexandra Heller-Nicholas wrote 'Ms. 45', published by Columbia University Press in 2017.
After Ms .45, Zoë Lund avoided being part of 'Abel's stable', but later turned up in Miami Vice and Special Effects (1984).
Barroom continuity slip: when the shoe salesman handles Thana's gun, the hammer is cocked, then not, and a shadow from the gun appears and disappears.
Ms .45 aired on Joe Bob Briggs' Joe Bob's Drive-In Theater on August 29, 1992, with guest Anita Rosenberg.
Riot grrrl band L7 wrote a song called 'Ms. 45', inspired by this movie.
A fan edited scenes from Ms .45 into an unofficial music video for John Maus's 'Streetlight' that went semi-viral and caught Maus's attention.
As Thana walks the neighbor's dog, a red truck rolls by with the name Ferrara on its front, a sly nod to director Abel Ferrara.
Jack McIntyre, Abel Ferrara's creative consultant on Ms .45, also played saxophone on the film's sleazy, sax-driven rock tracks.
At the party, the band's player mimes a trumpet but the music is saxophone, so the sound and the instrument don't match.
Abel Ferrara directed episodes of Miami Vice and Crime Story for his friend Michael Mann, who gives him editing tips in return for private screenings.
The 2000 U.S. DVD re-edit moved the killing of the man in the yellow T-shirt at the Halloween party offscreen. The 1983 U.S.A. Home Video VHS kept it uncut.
The Halloween party massacre is shot largely in slow motion, a flickering effect one reviewer says heightens the sense of psychotic delirium.
Ms .45 is namechecked in Bad Lieutenant, Machete, The Greasy Strangler and MaXXXine.
That one word, 'Sister', is the only thing Zoë Lund's mute character Thana says in the entire film.
